facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified
A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes, and intramedullary sclerosis, along with the presence of foamy histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells on biopsy, is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
Although the biopsy results do not support LCH, the patient's bone pain and radiographic findings could be seen in LCH, making it a consideration in the differential diagnosis.

The patient's elevated inflammatory markers and enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues could be seen in sarcoidosis, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

The patient's radiographic findings of bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes and intramedullary sclerosis could be seen in Paget's disease of bone, although the patient's age and lack of other characteristic features make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's biopsy results showing diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells support a diagnosis of histiocytosis, although the specific subtype is more likely to be Erdheim-Chester disease given the other clinical and radiographic findings.
